Medicaid’s collapse isn’t from funding cuts—it’s from decades of systemic theft. The program hemorrhages $55B annually in improper payments, duplicate services, and ER misuse by non-citizens. Hospitals like Wesley aren’t struggling because of reduced budgets; they’re drowning in bureaucratic bloat and unfunded mandates like Title VI translation services.

Real reform means cutting waste, not throwing more cash at a broken system. Prioritize Americans who paid into Medicaid—not those who broke the law to access it.

The Save America’s Rural Hospitals Act (H.R. 3684) throws $50B at rural facilities while Republicans slash $911B from Medicaid — a classic D.C. bait-and-switch. Hospitals aren’t collapsing from “cuts”; they’re drowning in bureaucracy. Section 106 proves the rot: wage index adjustments prioritize administrative tinkering over actual care.

Medicaid’s $55B annual fraud hemorrhage gets ignored while politicians scapegoat “funding gaps.” Real reform? Audit every dollar, purge duplicate programs, and jail price-gouging contractors.

Until then, temporary funds are just political theater — taxpayers fund the stage, bureaucrats take the bow.

Premiums are spiking because D.C. keeps propping up a broken system riddled with fraud and waste. The ACA’s temporary subsidies are a Band-Aid on a bullet wound—real reform means cutting Big Pharma’s price-gouging, ending Medicaid abuse by illegal immigrants, and exposing the corruption that drives costs.

Biden’s expansion locked in dependency; Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill slashes bureaucracy to prioritize patients over politics.

Fix the rot, don’t fund it.

The real issue isn’t funding—it’s systemic fraud and bureaucratic bloat. Medicaid’s collapse stems from millions added to the rolls through illegal immigration loopholes and administrative waste, not “cuts.” The One Big Beautiful Bill Act targets reckless spending on programs that prioritize non-citizens over taxpayers.

For example, Section 44142 exposes how states funnel billions into bloated contracts while ERs overflow with untracked usage. Premiums rise because D.C. protects pharma monopolies and hospital price-gouging instead of enforcing merit-based reforms.

Redirecting funds from failed bureaucracies to patient-first solutions isn’t cruelty—it’s accountability.

The numbers and legislative details behind this overhaul are laid bare here: https://t.co/cpmYxm765z

Skyline Healthcare’s concerns are valid—but not for the reasons RepFriedmanCA claims. Medicaid’s collapse isn’t from funding cuts; it’s from systemic theft. The HCBS Relief Act of 2025 pumps billions into “workforce development” (Section 2(d)(2)(J)) while ignoring Medicaid’s $55B annual improper payments.

Skyline’s patients suffer because bureaucrats prioritize bloated administrative contracts over actual care. Fraudulent billing, duplicate programs, and ER misuse by non-citizens drain resources—not Republican fiscal responsibility.

If RepFriedmanCA wants to “hold the line,” start auditing Medicaid’s $284B in HCBS spending instead of fearmongering. Real reform means cutting waste, not rubber-stamping D.C.’s money laundering.
